blocks.x: How long were you with Ambie?
Well I stayed with Ambie a long time.
You played with him for years.
Yeah, I stayed with Ambie. No, I stayed with Ambie about three years. We stayed down there. You was in there one night. Yeah. You and this drummer from Europe.
Yeah, they all came in there.
You were playing up there on the... Right, John. ...Chorst Street. Yeah, yeah. You used to play that quite often?
Yeah, we still played there...what else? Often and on.
Mm-hmm. It's a little bar. It was popular, wasn't it? Yeah, it's a nice place. Which farm? It's St. Claude. It's St. Claude and Kjellrack, I think. Somewhere around there.
That's right. That's right on St. Claude and Kjellrack.
Did you play...you used to play down the weekends or what? No, he just used to get up there.

Every once in a while. He moved further down. Oh, yeah? That's the one where...how do you call it? Son was playing drums, huh? Was that Luke Skiro? That Johnny's...right baby Steven's son was there? Joe Stevens, huh? I don't know. You see the band? Yeah, just Joe Stevens, the drummer.
The last time I heard Johnny had a white band.

Yeah, well that's... Luke Skiro was there. But that's the same place? Yeah, I think so. Maybe so. No, no, that's further down. That's another Johnny. I don't think it's the same... That's the same Johnny. This is the small place that you were talking about.
That's the same Johnny. He talking about the move further down. Yeah. Yeah. Little Austin Claude, further down. He had a white band and a nice band. But the trombone player and something else.
Yeah, but they got double trombone, valve trombone and trumpet. Yeah, yeah.
He used to play a long time with them. But what places did you play in with them? I don't know, I forgot. Jim.
